title: Mole cleans on manual runs; run logs pruned
result: a manual run calls `update_mole`, which runs the real `mo clean` with stdin closed (Mole's non-interactive path: user caches always, system caches when the cached sudo grant is live) and reports Mole's "Tracked cleanup" total as a change. Scheduled runs keep `report_mole`, dry run only. `cleanup-safety.sh` allows exactly that one call and its pattern now also catches `mo clean <redirect>`, which it used to miss. Compact runs keep the newest 30 `run-*.log` files. First real run freed 15.5 GB but Mole's user sweep (every child of `~/Library/Logs` and `~/Library/Caches`) deleted RocketUpdater's own log directory (events.log, 266 KB, unrecoverable; it had also happened on 2026-10-05 from a standalone `mo clean`) and lock directory mid-run. Created `~/.config/mole/whitelist` with Mole 1.59.1's defaults plus both RocketUpdater paths; `update_mole` now refuses to clean (status 20) unless that whitelist protects them. Second real run: 323.9 MB freed, logs and lock intact. Same whitelist installed on the Mac mini (Mole 1.57.0, identical defaults); its dry run lists both paths as protected and none of them as candidates.
evidence: `tests/plugins/mole.sh` and `tests/runner/run-log-pruning.sh` red on the previous code, green now; full regression suite green.
